key_terms.meaning: Steady stream from a nozzle; ideal velocity V = √(2gH) for head H.
Velocity of jet seen from a moving vane, V − u when the vane moves at u along the jet.

key_terms.term: Force on a moving curved vane
key_terms.meaning: F = ρ a (V − u)² (1 − cos θ), where θ is deflection angle, a jet area and ρ density.
W = F u, the force on the vane multiplied by the vane speed.
Vector diagram joining absolute velocity V, blade velocity u and relative velocity V_r.
Specific work = u₁V_u1 − u₂V_u2; head H_e = (u₁V_u1 − u₂V_u2)/g.
Torque on runner T = ρQ(r₁V_u1 − r₂V_u2); V_u is the whirl velocity component.
Turbine where pressure is constant across the runner and all head becomes jet kinetic energy; Pelton is one.
Turbine where pressure drops across the runner and part of the head acts as pressure; Francis and Kaplan are examples.
Impulse turbine with buckets on a wheel; used for high head, with speed ratio u/V about 0.5.
η_h = 2(u/V)(1 − u/V)(1 − cos φ), where φ is bucket exit angle; maximum near u/V = 0.5.
Mixed-flow reaction turbine for medium head; water enters radially and leaves axially.
Axial-flow reaction turbine for low head and large discharge; runner blades are adjustable.
Stationary vanes that give water whirl and control discharge into a reaction runner.
Diverging tube from runner exit to tailrace that recovers velocity head as pressure.
Ratio of pressure head recovered in the draft tube to velocity head at runner exit.
N_u = N/√H; speed of a geometrically similar turbine under 1 m head.
N_s = N√P/H<sup>5/4</sup>, with N in rpm, P in kW and H in m; used to choose turbine type.
η_h = runner work divided by water power supplied by the available head.
η_o = η_h η_m η_v = shaft power divided by water power.

takeaways: A jet force comes from momentum change and falls as the vane speed approaches the jet speed.
Euler's equation links turbine work to the change of angular momentum and the inlet and outlet velocity triangles.
Hydraulic turbines are classified by pressure action, flow direction and available head.
The Pelton wheel is an impulse turbine for high head, with best work near bucket speed equal to half jet speed.
Francis and Kaplan turbines are reaction turbines; pressure falls across the runner and a draft tube recovers exit kinetic energy.
A draft tube allows the runner to sit above tailwater while recovering velocity head as pressure.
Unit quantities and specific speed compare turbines without carrying size and head into every number.
Overall efficiency is the product of hydraulic, mechanical and volumetric efficiencies, and the operating point is where the turbine curve meets the site conditions.
bank_note: Long answers usually expect a labelled sketch, the momentum or Euler derivation, formulas with symbols defined, and a comparison or selection comment.

bank.q: Define an impulse turbine and a reaction turbine. Classify hydraulic turbines by pressure action, flow direction and head, with one example each.
outline: definitions of impulse and reaction action

bank.q: State Euler's turbomachine equation for a hydraulic turbine and explain each term using an inlet and outlet velocity triangle.
outline: meaning of u, V and V_u
energy transfer by angular momentum change

bank.q: Describe the main parts and working of a Pelton wheel, including the nozzle, runner, buckets and casing.
Explain the purpose of a draft tube and describe the common types with a simple sketch description.
Define unit speed, unit discharge, unit power and specific speed of a turbine; write their formulas.
Derive the force exerted by a jet on a moving curved vane and the work done per second. Show that for a Pelton bucket the hydraulic efficiency peaks near u/V = 0.5.
A Pelton wheel is supplied by a jet of velocity V and the bucket speed is u. Derive η_h and find the bucket speed for maximum efficiency when the bucket exit angle is φ.
Given inlet and outlet velocity triangle data for a Francis runner, use Euler's equation to compute the Euler head and hydraulic efficiency.
A draft tube has inlet velocity V₂ and outlet velocity V₃. Derive the pressure recovery and define draft tube efficiency.
Use specific speed to select a turbine for a site with given head and power. Explain the ranges for Pelton, Francis and Kaplan.
Compare Pelton, Francis and Kaplan turbines on head, discharge, flow direction, pressure action, efficiency and setting.
Evaluate how speed ratio and bucket exit angle affect Pelton wheel efficiency. Why is u/V = 0.5 not exactly reached in practice?
Analyze why a reaction turbine needs a draft tube and how draft tube design affects cavitation and setting above tailwater.
Explain turbine performance curves. How does the operating point change with load and guide-vane opening, and how is a turbine selected for a site?

glossary.def: Velocity of water measured from the fixed casing, denoted V.
Velocity of water measured from the moving runner, denoted V_r.
Runner speed at a point, u = πDN/60 for diameter D and speed N.
Diagram of V, u and V_r at inlet or outlet of a runner.
Head equivalent of work done by angular momentum change, H_e = (u₁V_u1 − u₂V_u2)/g.
Turbine in which pressure stays constant across the runner and the jet is free.
Turbine in which pressure falls across the runner and the runner is full of water.
Rotating part carrying buckets or blades that receives energy from water.
Curved cup on a Pelton runner that turns the jet and takes its momentum.
Stationary vane that controls flow and gives whirl before a reaction runner.
Diverging passage that connects runner exit to tailrace and recovers velocity head.
Channel that carries water away from the turbine after the draft tube.
Energy per unit weight of water available to the turbine, measured in metres.
Volume of water passing a section per second, measured in m³/s.
Ratio of work delivered to the runner to energy supplied by water.
Ratio of shaft power to runner power after bearing and seal losses.
Ratio of discharge through the runner to total discharge supplied.
Ratio of shaft power to water power, equal to the product of the three efficiencies.
Speed of a geometrically similar turbine that would give unit power under unit head.
Speed of a turbine under 1 m head, N_u = N/√H.
Discharge of a turbine under 1 m head, Q_u = Q/√H.
Power of a turbine under 1 m head, P_u = P/H<sup>3/2</sup>.
Ratio of runner speed to jet speed, u/V, about 0.5 for a Pelton wheel.
Ratio of flow velocity to runner speed at inlet of a reaction turbine.
Formation and collapse of vapour bubbles in low-pressure zones, causing erosion and noise.
Height of runner exit above tailrace; it affects pressure at runner exit.
